documents.title: Standards and Recommendations for the Use of Generative AI in Teaching and Learning at Northeastern
documents.summary: Provost-level standards and recommendations for using generative AI in teaching. It leaves the AI decision to instructors, asks them to state expectations in syllabi and assignments, and offers sample syllabus statements and assignment labels. It also sets conditions: university AI Policy compliance, review of tools, and review of AI grading of open-ended work.
documents.stance_why: The text says "the university supports faculty autonomy in determining appropriate AI use in their courses" and answers "No. It is up to each faculty member" on requiring AI. It offers sample statements (Encouraged, Sometimes Allowed, Not Permitted) and four assignment labels instead of one rule, so it delegates and lists tiers.

units.policy: Instructors are responsible for the quality and accuracy of the materials, including checking outputs for accuracy and making necessary revisions prior to sharing work with students.

documents.stance_why: The stub says the policy is "a framework for any faculty or staff member who is seeking to incorporate the use of AI", which welcomes AI use within a framework. No ban or instructor handoff appears, so permit; the page is thin and gives no conditions.

documents.title: Khoury College faculty on when — and when not — to use AI in the classroom
documents.summary: A college news article in which Khoury leaders and faculty describe their approach to AI in computing courses: fundamentals first, AI phased in later, instructors decide per assignment. It is not a formal policy but states a college principle of less or zero AI in introductory courses.
documents.stance_why: The article says "each Khoury instructor decides whether AI is forbidden, acceptable, suggested, or required for each assignment or project", so the college hands the decision to instructors, with guiding principles. It is a news item with no binding text, so delegates and its four categories are listed as tiers.

units.why: The dean says "We're AI-forward in our education", a college stance that welcomes AI, P02, though it still values fundamentals.
units.anchor: We’re AI-forward in our education

units.fit_note: Paired with "embracing our students learning the fundamentals"; stated by the dean in a news article, not as a rule.

units.anchor: crutch to coach to colleague
